case_title.quote: VUTUKURU LAKSHMAIAH v. STATE OF ANDHRA PRADESH
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

number_of_accused.quote: convicted A-1 to A-5 and A-7 to A-9
number_of_accused.reason: Accused A-1 to A-9 are referred to, consistent with nine accused.

accused_gender.reason: The judgment never states the accused's genders; 'Mixed' has no textual basis.

accused_age.reason: No accused age is stated in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of accused is not mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of accused is not mentioned.

accused_occupation.quote: was the Councilor for Ward No. 16 of Nellore Municipality

previous_criminal_record.reason: No criminal record of accused is mentioned.

victim_gender.quote: we find that he has named
victim_gender.reason: Deceased is referred to as male ('he') throughout.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Known to accused; political rivals with previous animosity; victim was witness against A-1
accused_victim_relationship.quote: the deceased was assaulted as he was a witness in Velongini Raja 's murder case wherein the accused-appellant, A-1, was an accused
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Judgment describes prior animosity and a witness relationship, not a stranger.

offence_category.reason: Offence is murder under Section 302 IPC.

statutory_provisions.quote: convicted A-1 to A-5 and A-7 to A-9 for the offences punishable under Sections 148 and 302 IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: Sections 148, 302, 324 and 324 read with 149 are all supported.

weapon.quote: stabbed the deceased multiple times with knives, while A-4 and A-6 beat him with iron rods
weapon.reason: Knives and iron rods are both stated as weapons.

evidence_type.quote: the dying declaration of the deceased
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness testimony and dying declaration are the evidence relied upon.

confession.reason: No confession by the accused is mentioned in the judgment.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: considering the nature of injuries and the previous animosity
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Previous animosity, multiple stab injuries and unlawful assembly are supported.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating circumstances are identified in the judgment.

trial_court_outcome.quote: convicted A-1 to A-5 and A-7 to A-9 for the offences punishable under Sections 148 and 302 IPC
trial_court_outcome.reason: Matches the trial court's convictions described.

high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court has acquitted A-4, A-8 and A-9
high_court_outcome.reason: Acquittal of A-4, A-8, A-9 and upheld conviction of others is stated.

final_outcome.quote: we do not perceive any merit in these appeals and accordingly, the same stand dismissed

offence_finally_established.quote: it is not a fit case where the offence under Section 302 IPC should be converted to Section 304 Part I IPC
offence_finally_established.reason: Murder under Section 302 IPC is upheld.

imprisonment_years.reason: No term in years is stated; life imprisonment is given.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Facts summary without the appellate outcome or the statement that arguments were rejected
neutral_facts.quote: The Supreme Court affirmed the High Court's decision, finding that the evidence... was reliable
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are largely accurate but the summary reveals the Supreme Court's outcome, which is prohibited.

offence_severity.reason: Life imprisonment is the sentence stated for the Section 302 conviction.

attempt_completion.reason: The victim died, so the offence was completed.

physical_harm.quote: there are five stab injuries at different parts of the body
physical_harm.reason: Multiple stab injuries leading to death three days later are supported.

number_of_offences.reason: The judgment does not state a count of 8 charged or 7 upheld offences.

financial_property_loss.reason: Property or financial loss is not discussed in the judgment.

premeditation_planning.quote: considering the nature of injuries and the previous animosity
premeditation_planning.reason: Court inferred intent from injuries and animosity; it did not find premeditation.

motive.quote: considering the nature of injuries and the previous animosity
motive.reason: Previous animosity is identified as the motive context.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the witnesses have categorically deposed that they were able to see the accused persons
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Eyewitness PW-2 and PW-3 testimony and the dying declaration were accepted.

witness_credibility.quote: we are unable to put them in the category of so-called 'chance witnesses'
witness_credibility.reason: Court found witnesses credible despite lighting claims and not chance witnesses.

post_offence_conduct.reason: Post-offence conduct of accused is not discussed.

trial_duration.correct_value: Offence 14.05.1996; High Court judgment 22.03.2007; Supreme Court decision 24.04.2015; trial judgment date not stated
trial_duration.quote: The present appeals are directed against the judgment and order dated 22.03.2007
trial_duration.reason: The 22.03.2007 date is the High Court's judgment; trial judgment date is not stated.

legal_representation.quote: Nagendra Rai, A.TM. Rangaramanujam, P. N. Ramalingam, for the Appellant
legal_representation.reason: Counsel for appellant and respondent are listed correctly.

investigation_status.quote: After completion of the investigation, the chargesheet was placed before the competent court

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Non-framing of charge under Section 149 IPC was raised; court held it caused no prejudice
procedural_irregularity.quote: the charge framed against the appellants was simplicitor Section 302 IPC
procedural_irregularity.reason: Judgment discusses the s.149 charge omission as an irregularity raised, not 'none noted'.

appeal_history.quote: partly allowed the appeal thereby acquitting A4, A5 and A9
appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction, partial High Court acquittal and Supreme Court dismissal are stated.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Prosecution also argued conviction with aid of s.149 was permissible without a charge, and that the offence was squarely s.302
prosecution_argument.quote: there is no bar, regard being had to the evidence on record, to convict the accused-appellants with the aid of the said provision
prosecution_argument.reason: Most points are supported, but the s.149 no-bar argument is omitted.

defence_argument.correct_value: Defence also argued lack of intention, alibi and Water Committee attendance; s.149 conviction not permissible without charge
defence_argument.quote: the appellants could not have been convicted in aid of Section 149 IPC as the charge framed against them was simplicitor Section 302 IPC
defence_argument.reason: Chance witnesses, vague dying declaration and false implication are supported; alibi and no-intention arguments are omitted.

legal_principle_applied.quote: the burden shifts to the accused to establish the plea of alibi with certainty
legal_principle_applied.reason: Non-fatality of missing s.149 charge, alibi burden and dying declaration reliability are all applied.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Also referred: State of Orissa v. Dibakar Naik, Sunder Lal v. State of Rajasthan, Marimuthu v. State of Tamil Nadu
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Willie (William) Slaney v. State of M.P.
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Listed cases are supported, but three referred cases in the headnote (para 20) are omitted.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Not stated as a sentencing rationale; court declined s.304 Part I conversion given injuries and previous animosity
sentencing_rationale.quote: considering the nature of injuries and the previous animosity, we are of the considered opinion that it is not a fit case
sentencing_rationale.reason: Judgment gives reasoning for refusing conversion, so 'Not applicable' is inaccurate.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No mitigating factors are identified by the court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Nature of five stab injuries and previous animosity (victim a witness against A-1)
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: considering the nature of injuries and the previous animosity
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court expressly relied on injuries and animosity as factors against conversion.

other_sentence_order.correct_value: All sentences to run concurrently; separate sentence under s.148
other_sentence_order.quote: all the sentences shall be concurrent
other_sentence_order.reason: Judgment states sentences are concurrent, contradicting 'None'.
